text:
ara: Heads-up — prod-privregion (ap-south-2a) nodes failing to join after the egress policy change. Keystore/KMS decrypt errors in node boot logs.
ops-bot: Alert: instance-boot-failures x23 in prod-privregion (ap-south-2a). Ticket auto-created: ALERT-8921.
samir: seeing repeated: "Failed to call KMS: AccessDenied" and also timeouts. excerpt from /var/log/redwood/node.log -> 
    Mar 20 14:15:32 node-12 redwood-node[1]: error: kms decrypt: dial tcp 10.0.5.23:443: i/o timeout

marta: FYI I merged the new graded-egress policy (PR #4217) at 14:02 UTC to tighten outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 for private regions. It was supposed to allow outbound to kms.* hostnames only.
doug: rolling back now but want a narrower mitigation before full revert. We can't keep wide open 0/0 long-term.
marta: snippet of the deployed policy (simplified):
```json
{
  "egress": [
    {"dest": "0.0.0.0/0", "port": 443, "action": "deny"},
    {"dest": "kms.ap-south-2.amazonaws.com", "port": 443, "action": "allow"}
  ]
}
```
samir: problem: our keystore sits behind privatelink -> keystore.svc.privnet resolves to private ENI IPs (10.0.5.0/24). Allowlist-by-hostname doesn't catch ENI IPs so the rule blocked traffic. That explains timeouts (traffic never hits public KMS hostnames).
ara: exact boot failure trace (condensed):
[LOG] 2026-03-20T14:15:32Z node-12: join attempt -> keystore decrypt failed -> dial tcp 10.0.5.23:443: i/o timeout -> node join aborted.
doug: temp mitigation: adding an allow rule for the privatelink ENI CIDR 10.0.5.0/24 in the ap-south-2a VPC egress policy. Applying to that AZ only as canary. Running: `terraform apply -var region=ap-south-2a -target=module.egress_allow_privlink`
ops-bot: Deploy started by doug (CI #8763). Plan success, applying change to infra-ap-south-2a.
samir: nodes are rejoining. Warm pool dipped but we recovered ~+10 GPUs back online within 8 minutes of the change. Boot failures dropped to 0 for canary cohort.
ara: cost note: adding the NAT/backdoor for privatelink IPs increases outbound NAT usage for that AZ — rough estimate ~$170/day if left wide for the whole region.
marta: agreed we can't keep blanket ENI allow forever. Follow-up: we need a deterministic mapping of privatelink ENIs for keystore + reconcile CIDRs during policy deploys. Also update audit logs so this traffic is visible. Right now it looked like "no external KMS traffic" which hid the root cause.
doug: I'll open an RFC with design options: 1) maintain managed allowlist of privatelink ENIs updated by a controller; 2) use security-group-based allowlists linked to endpoint ENIs; 3) route KMS calls over a dedicated VPC endpoint that keeps hostnames consistent.
samir: one immediate thing — enable ENI flow logs to our SIEM for privatelink ENIs (sample=100%) so we can see egress attempts in future and attach to audit. Today the flow logs weren't capturing due to sampling + retention settings.
ara: rollback to previous policy completed at 14:28 UTC (revert PR #4217). Monitoring window until 15:00 UTC. Marking incident SEV3.
marta: created ticket INF-2248: "privatelink ENI-aware egress policy + audit capture". Owners: @eng-platform, @eng-security. Assigned to doug and samir. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Alert resolved: instance-boot-failures (23 -> 0). Closed at 14:29 UTC.
doug: follow-up action: I'll prototype a controller that queries privatelink endpoints, extracts ENI IPs, and pushes a minimal allowlist via terraform-provider-api. Will demo Thurs 09:30 PT.
samir: FYI I'll also adjust flow log sampling and create a low-cost retention tier for these ENI logs so we can triage faster next time.
ara: thanks all. Action items recap in thread: 1) doug — RFC + proto for ENI reconciliation; 2) samir — flow log sampling + retention change; 3) marta — coordinate a hardened egress deployment plan with canary and audit; 4) ops — monitor GPU warm pool and cost delta. I'll write the short postmortem and link here when ready.
doug: ping me if you want to join the design review. I'll post calendar invite.
samir: closing thread for now — will post postmortem link INF-2248/pm when done.
